result:
result: not merge-ready; one blocking regression (Bun lookup fallback dropped), the rest non-blocking.

changed: none (read-only). `packages/integrations/claude/build.ts` and `packages/integrations/pi/build.ts` produced no diff, so the dist files match a fresh build.

checks:
- `bun test packages/integrations/pi/tests/extension.test.ts packages/integrations/pi/tests/pi.test.ts packages/runtime/tests/pi/tools.test.ts` -> exit 0, 307 pass, 0 fail.
- Both build scripts, then `git status --short` -> clean.
- I did not run `mise run verify`, and I ran no pi, Windows or T3 Code. Everything about Windows is read from the code and its win32-stubbed tests.
- The built-in `/code-review` (high) ran. I checked each of its 7 findings against the code.

blockers:
1. **Bun lookup regression.** `packages/integrations/pi/src/extension.ts:706-709` now runs `exec(signal, "bun", [...bundled, ...])`, so bare `bun` must be on the PATH of Pi's process. The `sh` wrapper it replaced also tried `${BUN_INSTALL:-$HOME/.bun}/bin/bun` (`packages/integrations/pi/dist/scripts/holyagent`, lines 28-33).
   - Failure: Bun is installed in `~/.bun/bin` and put on PATH only by a shell rc file, and Pi starts from a GUI or an editor such as T3 Code. The old path worked through that fallback. The new one fails to spawn, so every `holyagent` call returns CommandFailed and the config, status and state collection all fail.
   - Fix: resolve bun with the same fallback before `exec`, or pass the resolved absolute path.
   - Tests would not notice: they stub `pi.exec`, and `extension.test.ts` asserts only `command === "bun"`.

non-blocking:
- `packages/runtime/src/pi/tools.ts:12,18`: `powershell` is allowlisted for specialists on every platform. In the installed Pi, `powershell` is registered everywhere and only throws when called off Windows ("only available on Windows"), so a Linux or macOS specialist is shown a tool that always errors. The allowlist and exclusion matchers ignore unregistered names, so nothing breaks at launch. This is the same selection and exclusions as `bash`, as the Assignment asks, so it is a trade-off, not a defect. The root avoids it with the Windows-only `+powershell`.
- Model-facing text (`kimi-k3.1/root/dispatch.md:3`, `delegating.md:9`) still tells the model to run the extensionless `sh` wrapper through bash. On Windows without Git Bash, `powershell` cannot run it, so the model's own `holyagent` calls (`intent`, `assignment`, `status`) still need Git Bash. The extension's own calls work. `docs/pi/orchestration.md` says "the wrapper stays for the model's own shell calls", so this is a known gap. Prompts that name the `bun ... holyagent.js` form would close it.
- `extension.test.ts` (around line 499) checks the wrapper's flags only as three substrings of its last line. A flag added to `wrapper.sh` later would not fail it. One shared constant would remove the duplicate.
- Rejected: the cmd.exe injection claim. The provider is a literal enum and model ids are limited to `[A-Za-z0-9._:/@+-]`. Rejected: the claim that the 9009 check applies to every command. It sits in `checkProvider`, whose runner is used only by the `pi` probes. Rejected: matching cmd.exe's "not recognized" stderr. It exits 9009, which is handled and tested.
- Tests are not weakened. Each new behavior has a test: runtime args, cmd.exe wrapping, the 9009 handling, the root gaining `powershell` only on Windows, and `powershell` selected and excluded wherever `bash` is.

verdict: not merge-ready until the Bun fallback is restored. No other blocker found.
